title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-01-30
lineage: SBD > MR > C > DAT > CDR > EAC(secure) > Cool Edit (minor fixes) > CD Wave (retracking) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Solid soundboard capture of a historic early‑1970 show with razor‑sharp Jerry leads and standout performances of High Time, Easy Wind, The Other One and Black Peter.
ai_review.review: The recording is generally clear and well‑balanced, though a few listeners note it isn’t as pristine as some SBD expectations. Musically the concert shines – reviewers rave about Jerry Garcia’s sharp leads, the atmospheric High Time and Easy Wind, a smoking The Other One segueing into Cosmic Charlie, plus strong renditions of Black Peter and China Cat Sunflower. Overall the show is considered an underrated gem from this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviews are enthusiastic (5‑star) praising both performance and sound; average star rating ~3.8 with strong positive language pushes the AI rating into the high‑four range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear, crisp and well‑balanced; several reviewers call the sound great, though one notes it isn’t as immaculate as some SBD purists expect.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers describe an organized‑chaos first half that settles into a mellow groove, with tight transitions (notably The Other One → Cosmic Charlie) and strong acoustic moments that keep the momentum flowing.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Leads described as razor‑sharp, perfect tone and atmospheric; multiple reviewers highlight his guitar work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s last show – noted as muddled at times but shines on China Cat Sunflower and High Time.
